title: Bernard Goldberg financing the first band
summary: Goldberg gave $1,000 and uniforms to start the band in 1929; later bookers failed and Albert booked himself.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: What about this Bernard Goldberg? Had you get in touch with him?

Well, Bernard Goldberg was an admirer of, he admired my playing and he thought that I would make a band leader. And he would come to Shadowland and he would ask me to organize a band. So I told him I wasn't ready. And when I came back here to New Orleans in, oh, it was 1929. But, Bernard came over and he said, why don't you get a band together? He says, I get you a real good job to start off with. I said, well, that sounds all right. He says, you need any money? He says, I'll give you a thousand dollars. So he gave me a thousand dollars. I got around here and got these guys together and they all decided it was a good deal. The first job was to stay for him in Dallas. And we all had brand new uniforms. Goldberg bought all of that. And I wish it would have been possible that I could have stayed with him because I believe if Goldberg had stayed with us, it would have been feasible for him and profitable for all of us. Because right behind him, we got another one named, oh, he's here in this town, Rabinowitz. He's mind the tire business, the men's wear tire. You might have met old Benowitz. He has a place right up there on where old Rampo Street used to come in. I don't know.
Well, if you don't know him, so much the better.
So you try a lot of different bookers and you book the band yourself on judging from what you stand. That's right.
Well, you see, when the bookers would do bad and get rid of the bookers, then I had to go ahead and book them all.
